questions.question: State any three merits of roadways.
answer_steps: Construction cost is much lower than that of railway lines, and roads can cross dissected, undulating and mountainous terrain.
Road transport is economical for a few persons and small amounts of goods over short distances, with door-to-door service and low loading costs.
Roads act as feeders to other modes, linking railway stations, airports and sea ports.

questions.question: Where and why is rail transport the most convenient means of transportation?
answer_steps: Rail transport is most convenient in the northern plains.
The plains have vast level land, so construction is easy.
They also have high population density and rich agricultural resources, giving plenty of passengers and freight.

questions.question: What is the significance of the border roads?
answer_steps: The Border Roads Organisation (1960) builds roads in the northern and north-eastern border areas.
These roads are of strategic importance for defence.
They improve accessibility in difficult terrain and help the economic development of border areas.

questions.question: What is meant by trade? What is the difference between international and local trade?
answer_steps: Trade is the exchange of goods among people, states and countries; the market is where it happens.
Local trade is carried on in cities, towns and villages within a country.
International trade is carried on between two or more countries, through sea, air or land routes.

questions.question: Why are the means of transportation and communication called the lifelines of a nation and its economy?
answer_steps: Transport moves raw materials to factories and finished goods to markets, linking producers and consumers.
It moves people for work, trade and tourism across the country.
Communication carries information quickly, helping business, administration and services.
Together they connect remote areas, reduce regional imbalance and help national integration.
They support international trade through ports and airports, so the economy cannot function without them.

questions.question: Write a note on the changing nature of the international trade in the last fifteen years.
answer_steps: International trade has grown, and India now trades with all major trading blocks and regions of the world.
Exports have diversified into engineering goods, chemicals, gems and jewellery and petroleum products, besides agricultural products and minerals.
India has emerged as a software giant, earning large foreign exchange from information technology services.
Imports include petroleum and crude products, machinery, electronics, chemicals and gems.
Better ports, airports and communication have made trade faster, and services trade has grown alongside goods.

questions.question: Why was Haldia port developed?

questions.question: Why is air transport important for the north-eastern states?
answer_steps: The north-east has difficult terrain of hills, forests and rivers.
Air transport covers such terrain with ease and has made access to the region much easier.

questions.question: Describe any three major sea ports of India's west coast.
answer_steps: Kandla (Gujarat): the first port developed after Independence to ease trade on Mumbai after Karachi went to Pakistan; a tidal port.
Mumbai (Maharashtra): the biggest port, with a spacious natural and well-sheltered harbour.
Marmagao (Goa): the premier iron ore exporting port (also New Mangalore for Kudremukh ore, and Kochi at a lagoon).

questions.question: Describe the three important pipeline networks of India.
answer_steps: From upper Assam to Kanpur (UP) via Guwahati, Barauni and Allahabad, with branches to Haldia and Siliguri.
From Salaya (Gujarat) to Jalandhar (Punjab) via Viramgam, Mathura, Delhi and Sonipat.
The HVJ gas pipeline from Hazira (Gujarat) via Vijaipur (MP) to Jagdishpur (UP), with branches to Kota, Shahjahanpur and Babrala.

questions.question: Describe the classification of roads in India.
answer_steps: Golden Quadrilateral super highways link Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai; N-S (Srinagar–Kanyakumari) and E-W (Silchar–Porbandar) corridors; built by NHAI.
National highways link extreme parts of the country; Sher-Shah Suri Marg (Delhi–Amritsar) is NH 1.
State highways link state capitals with district headquarters; maintained by the State PWD.
District roads link district headquarters with other places (Zila Parishad); rural roads link villages with towns under PMGSY.
Border roads built by the Border Roads Organisation (1960) serve strategic northern and north-eastern border areas.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"Kandla in Kuchchh was the first port developed soon after Independence to ease the volume of trade on the Mumbai port, in the wake of loss of Karachi port to Pakistan after the Partition. Kandla, also known as the Deendayal Port, is a tidal port."* (NCERT)

(i) Why was Kandla port developed? (1)

(ii) What type of port is Kandla? (1)

(iii) Name two other major ports on the west coast and one fact about each. (2)
answer_steps: (i) To ease trade on Mumbai port after Karachi port went to Pakistan at Partition.
(ii) A tidal port.
(iii) Any two: Mumbai has the biggest natural harbour; Marmagao is the premier iron ore port; New Mangalore exports Kudremukh ore; Kochi is at the entrance of a lagoon.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"Exports and imports are the components of trade. The balance of trade of a country is the difference between its export and import. When the value of export exceeds the value of imports, it is called a favourable balance of trade."* (NCERT)

(i) What are the two components of trade? (1)

(ii) What is an unfavourable balance of trade? (1)

(iii) Name two goods India exports and two it imports. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Exports and imports.
(ii) When the value of imports exceeds the value of exports.
(iii) Exports: gems and jewellery, engineering goods, chemicals, agricultural products, petroleum products; imports: petroleum and crude products, machinery, electronic items, gems (any two each).
